official.deadline_note: Alberta Student Aid publishes no deadline. The official policy manual states: 'To inquire about the deadline date and application process, contact the Student Awards Office at your post-secondary institution.'
official.application_cycle: Fall 2026 and/or Winter 2027 terms (current eligibility wording on the official page)
official.status_note: The official page currently lists eligibility for enrolment in the Fall 2026 and/or Winter 2027 term; institutions select recipients, and scholarship payments must be made prior to March 1.
benefits: Minimum award of $11,000 and maximum of $15,000
Funded through the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund
Open to international students as well as Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents and Protected Persons
Established to incent the best and the brightest students, including international students, to study in Alberta
Scholarship payments must be made prior to March 1
eligibility: Be enrolled full-time in a master's, doctoral, or graduate level program; graduate level programs must be able to ladder into a master's degree program
Be enrolled in at least 60% of a full course load (40% of a full course load if you are a student with a permanent disability) in at least one term of study in a graduate program
Be enrolled in the Fall 2026 and/or Winter 2027 term
Be living in Alberta while studying at an eligible Alberta post-secondary institution
Be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident of Canada or Protected Person, OR an international student, OR a Status Indian/First Nations, Non-Status Indian/First Nations, Metis or Inuit
requirements: Nomination: students studying in-province are nominated by the Student Awards Offices at eligible Alberta public post-secondary institutions
Meet the minimum eligibility criteria for the Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship plus any additional eligibility criteria set by the school
selection_criteria: Outstanding academic achievement of students pursuing graduate studies in Alberta (stated purpose of the scholarship)
Schools select recipients based on the minimum eligibility criteria for the Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship and any additional eligibility criteria set by the school
coverage: Award value of minimum $11,000 and maximum $15,000 (CAD); the official pages state only the value and do not state what the money covers
application_method: For more information on how to apply, contact the Student Awards or Scholarships Offices at your school, or visit your school's website
To inquire about the deadline date and application process, contact the Student Awards Office at your post-secondary institution
official.application_route: Nomination-based: apply through your Alberta institution's Student Awards or Scholarships Office; there is no direct application to Alberta Student Aid.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be living in Alberta while studying at an eligible Alberta post-secondary institution and meet one of: Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident of Canada or Protected Person; international student; or Status Indian/First Nations, Non-Status Indian/First Nations, Metis or Inuit.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. International students are explicitly eligible provided they are living in Alberta while studying at an eligible Alberta post-secondary institution.
official.description: The Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship recognizes outstanding academic achievement of students pursuing graduate studies in Alberta. It was established to incent the best and the brightest students, including international students, to study in Alberta, and is funded through the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund.
official.program_type: Provincial scholarship funded through the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund

applicant_utility.summary: The AGES is a nomination-driven provincial award worth $11,000-$15,000 CAD for full-time master's and doctoral students at eligible Alberta institutions, and you cannot apply for it directly - your school's Student Awards Office nominates you, so the real competition happens at the faculty level in the fall. Because the province publishes no deadline and requires payments to be made before March 1, institutional nomination cut-offs land earlier in the academic year and differ from school to school. International students are explicitly eligible, but you must be living in Alberta while enrolled, and your program must be a master's, doctoral, or graduate-level program able to ladder into a master's degree. Treat the award as a one-time boost toward study costs rather than full funding, since the official pages never state that tuition or living expenses are covered.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving full-time graduate students (including international students) already enrolled at an Alberta public institution who can win a nomination from their faculty or awards office.
application_readiness_checklist: Email your institution's Student Awards or Scholarships Office in early fall to ask for this cycle's AGES nomination deadline and process, and copy your graduate coordinator
Confirm your program qualifies: master's, doctoral, or graduate level with a ladder into a master's degree, at an eligible Alberta post-secondary institution
Verify your enrolment meets at least 60% of a full course load (40% with a permanent disability) in a graduate program in the Fall 2026 and/or Winter 2027 term
Keep an up-to-date transcript, CV and (for thesis students) a short research or program-goals statement ready for your faculty's internal nomination package
Make sure your records show you are living in Alberta while studying, as residency in-province is a stated eligibility condition
common_rejection_risks: Never being nominated - the awards office only sees students put forward by faculties, so quietly waiting for a provincial deadline means missing the award entirely
Enrolling below the 60% full-course-load threshold (or 40% if you have a permanent disability) in the qualifying term
Being in a graduate-level program that cannot ladder into a master's degree, which makes you ineligible regardless of grades
Not living in Alberta while studying, which breaks the residency condition even with top marks
Missing your institution's internal nomination cut-off, which is the only deadline that actually applies and is set school by school
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, living expenses, and any travel or relocation costs: the official pages publish only a flat $11,000-$15,000 value and make no coverage statement, so applicants must fund everything else themselves.
document_audit: The awarding body publishes no document list, so the package is whatever your institution asks for - commonly a student declaration form, transcripts, a CV, and a research proposal or program-goals statement for thesis-based students
Institution-specific criteria and forms differ across Alberta schools, so request the current internal nomination package rather than relying on another university's list
If you change institutions or programs mid-cycle, contact the awards office at the school you currently attend - eligibility is determined there
alerts: No provincial deadline exists: your school's internal nomination date is the only date that matters, and it typically falls well before the province's March 1 payment cut-off
Current-cycle eligibility is worded around the Fall 2026 and/or Winter 2027 terms, so enrolment timing in those specific terms matters
The award is selected by each institution against its own additional criteria on top of the provincial minimums, so strength of competition varies by school and faculty
Funding is a fixed scholarship value with no published coverage of tuition or living costs - budget for the full cost of graduate study independently
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You never file with Alberta Student Aid: your faculty or department builds the nomination package and the institution's Student Awards Office nominates you, with the province then confirming payment.
